arxiv-2107-02412.title: GBLinks: GNN-Based Beam Selection and Link Activation for Ultra-dense D2D mmWave Networks
arxiv-2107-02412.creator: Shiwen He, Shaowen Xiong, Wei Zhang, Yiting Yang, Ju Ren, Yongming Huang
arxiv-2107-02412.description: Abstract In this paper, we consider the problem of joint beam selection and link activation across a set of communication pairs to effectively control the interference between communication pairs via inactivating part communication pairs in ultra-dense device-to-device (D2D) mmWave communication networks. The resulting optimization problem is formulated as an integer programming problem that is nonconvex and NP-hard.

arxiv-2110-00559.title: Nonadiabatic Fluctuations and the Charge-Density-Wave Transition in One-Dimensional Electron-Phonon Systems: a Dynamic Self-Consistent Theory
arxiv-2110-00559.creator: Alain Moïse Dikandé 1, and Claude Bourbonnais 2
arxiv-2110-00559.description: Abstract The Peierls instability in one-dimensional electron-phonon systems is known to be qualitatively well described by the Mean-Field theory, however the related self-consistent problem so far has only been able to predict a partial suppression of the transition even with proper account of classical lattice fluctuations.

arxiv-2503-23044.title: CityGS- 𝒳 \mathcal{X} : A Scalable Architecture for Efficient and Geometrically Accurate Large-Scale Scene Reconstruction
arxiv-2503-23044.creator: Yuanyuan Gao, Hao Li, Jiaqi Chen, Zhengyu Zou, Zhihang Zhong, Dingwen Zhang, Xiao Sun, Junwei Han
arxiv-2503-23044.description: Abstract Despite its significant achievements in large-scale scene reconstruction, 3D Gaussian Splatting still faces substantial challenges, including slow processing, high computational costs, and limited geometric accuracy. These core issues arise from its inherently unstructured design and the absence of efficient parallelization.

arxiv-2505-00162.title: Stochastic Subspace Descent Accelerated via Bi-fidelity Line Search
arxiv-2505-00162.creator: Nuojin Cheng nuojin.cheng@colorado.edu, Alireza Doostan alireza.doostan@colorado.edu, Stephen Becker stephen.becker@colorado.edu
arxiv-2505-00162.description: Abstract Efficient optimization remains a fundamental challenge across numerous scientific and engineering domains, especially when objective function and gradient evaluations are computationally expensive. While zeroth-order optimization methods offer effective approaches when gradients are inaccessible, their practical performance can be limited by the high cost associated with function queries.

arxiv-2601-12812.title: Do Clinical Question Answering Systems Really Need Specialised Medical Fine Tuning?
arxiv-2601-12812.creator: Sushant Kumar Ray, Gautam Siddharth Kashyap, Sahil Tripathi, Nipun Joshi, [-0.4ex] Vijay Govindarajan, Rafiq Ali, Jiechao Gao, Usman Naseem, [-0.4ex] Jamia Hamdard, New Delhi, India, [-0.4ex] Cornell University, New York, USA, [-0.4ex] Expedia Group, USA, [-0.4ex] DSEU-Okhla, New Delhi, India, [-0.4
arxiv-2601-12812.description: Abstract Clinical Question-Answering (CQA) industry systems are increasingly rely on Large Language Models (LLMs), yet their deployment is often guided by the assumption that domain-specific fine-tuning is essential. Although specialised medical LLMs such as BioBERT, BioGPT, and PubMedBERT remain popular, they face practical limitations including narrow coverage, high retraining costs, and limited adaptability.

pmc-10647842.title: Association between Lipids, Apolipoproteins and Telomere Length: A Mendelian Randomization Study
pmc-10647842.creator: Gehua Zhu, Jiamin Xu, Guanghua Guo, Feng Zhu, Manohar Garg, Markus Herrmann
pmc-10647842.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). (1) Background: The relationship between lipids, apolipoproteins, and telomere length (TL) has been explored in previous studies; however, the causal relationship between the two remains unclear. This study aims to assess the causal relationship between lipids, apolipoproteins, and TL using the two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) approach; (2) Methods: This study comprehensively employed both univariate MR (uvMR) and multivariate MR (mvMR) methods to genetically evaluate the associations between 21 exposures related to lipids and apolipoproteins and the outcome of TL.

pmc-11409223.title: Forced air oscillations – pneumatic capacitance in microfluidic oscillators produces non-linear responses and emergent behaviors†
pmc-11409223.creator: Sasha Cai Lesher-Pérez, Vishwa Vasani, Jihye So, Shuichi Takayama
pmc-11409223.description: Pneumatic control mechanisms have long been integral to microfluidic systems, primarily using solenoid valves, pressurized gases, and vacuums to direct liquid flow. Despite advancements in liquid-driven self-regulated microfluidic circuits, gas-driven systems leveraging fluid compressibility remain underexplored. This study presents a mathematical and experimental investigation of gas-driven microfluidic circuits, focusing on forced-air oscillators.

pmc-11433730.title: A Novel High Performance Liquid Chromatography Method for Camphor Determination and Application in Cosmetics and Pharmaceuticals: Development and Validation
pmc-11433730.creator: Martin Lalić, Ana Soldić, Zdenka Lalić, Miranda Sertić
pmc-11433730.description: A novel high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) method with 4-N,N-dimethylaminobenzaldehyde as an internal standard was developed for the determination of Camphor with the main goal of facilitating the analysis of different cosmetic and pharmaceutical products that contain Camphor in analytical laboratories. The method can be applied to cosmetic and pharmaceutical samples such as gels, ointments, and creams containing Camphor.

pmc-12594841.title: The transcription factor ZEB2 mediates the antitumor efficacy of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes in non–small cell lung cancer
pmc-12594841.creator: Jiajia Wang, Fei Liu, Yongyong Li, Jiaojiao Gao, Shasha Yang, Mei Tian, Lili Deng, Yan Yang, Beilei Gong, Chengling Zhao, Huiyuan Gong, Zongyu Xie, Yongchun Zhou, Rongzhong Huang, Qiang Luo, Depeng Jiang, Xiaojing Wang
pmc-12594841.description: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) offers an in vivo approach to activate CD8+ tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (CD8+TILs) in cases of advanced non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). A large fraction of NSCLC patients is unresponsive to ICBs and relapse due to the development of dysfunctional CD8+TILs with impaired cytotoxicity.
